sources.title: LinuxGSM info_game.sh (fn_info_game_ct reads no rcon key)
antimodes201/craftopia-server - Docker container for a Craftopia Server

notes: Craftopia's dedicated server (Steam tool app 1670340, confirmed independently by LinuxGSM's appid="1670340" and by craftopia-docker's steamcmd +app_update 1670340; Unity headless, ./Craftopia.x86_64 launched with -batchmode -showlogs) exposes no command channel: no RCON, no admin HTTP/REST API, and no documented console verb. Its configuration surface is ServerSetting.ini (LinuxGSM sets servercfg="ServerSetting.ini"; the antimodes201 README spells it ServerSettings.ini). The keys observed across independent tooling are name, difficulty, gameMode, port, bindAddress, maxPlayerNumber, usePassword, serverPassword, autoSaveSec and autoSavePerHour - craftopia-docker's entrypoint writes nine of them and LinuxGSM's fn_info_game_ct additionally reads bindAddress. No source enumerates the file authoritatively, so treat that list as the observed union rather than as provably complete; what matters here is that no observed key is an RCON enable/port/password setting and none is an admin, whitelist or ban-list setting. Two further LinuxGSM signals corroborate: ctserver's _default.cfg contains no rcon lines at all, and info_game.sh's fn_info_game_ct reads no rcon key even though the same file reads rconport/rconpassword for RCON-capable games in ~70 places. LinuxGSM also sets querymode="1" (session only), i.e. it attempts no game query protocol against Craftopia. Default game port is 6587 TCP/UDP per the antimodes201 wrapper (GAME_PORT=6587, published as 6587/udp and 6587/tcp); LinuxGSM hardcodes no default and reads port from the ini. Caveat on the one ambiguous signal: LinuxGSM sets stopmode="5", which command_stop.sh implements as fn_stop_graceful_cmd "stop" 30 - tmux send-keys "stop", wait up to 30s, then fall back to fn_stop_tmux. That is a best-effort shutdown attempt common to Unity headless servers and is not evidence of an admin console; no listPlayers/kick/ban/say verb has ever been published for it, so no stdin commands are recorded. Craftopia does have an in-game cheat/command text box, but that is a CLIENT-side console for item spawning and is unreachable from the server host, so it cannot be used for moderation. Confidence is low rather than high because Pocketpair publishes no dedicated-server documentation that could be located; this is a negative finding resting on agreement-by-absence across independent server-management tooling, not on an explicit publisher statement. Kick and ban therefore have to fall through to the host-level floor (firewall / network layer).
